name: AbilityNet My Computer My Way
description: A free AbilityNet guide to accessibility features built into common computers, tablets and smartphones, organised around vision, hearing, motor and cognitive access needs.
intended_use: Find step-by-step ways to change built-in device settings when reading, attention, memory, dexterity, movement or other access needs make technology harder to use.
audience_or_context: Disabled and neurodivergent people, families, supporters and anyone who wants to make a mainstream device easier to use without first buying specialist software.
limitations: Available settings depend on the device, operating-system version and app being used, so instructions can become outdated as software changes.
Built-in accessibility settings may not be sufficient for every access need and the guide is not an assessment of an individual's requirements.
cost_or_access_notes: AbilityNet describes My Computer My Way as free to use.
conflicts_of_interest: The resource is produced by AbilityNet and described from AbilityNet's own pages; ND Oracle records its function and access route without treating first-party benefit statements as independent evidence.

provenance.method: AbilityNet and My Computer My Way official pages checked on 2026-08-28. Listing records the current free guide, supported access areas and update dependency without adding efficacy claims.
